title: Dispatch BBA 5: Hospital Fire Records Conceal a Forty Second Patient
summary: A family record identifies the child who rang the alarm and escaped.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Retired dressmaker Eleanor Arden, aged sixty-one, came to the Institute yesterday with a small brass clapper she said had belonged to her grandmother. The clapper was stamped with the mark of the bell foundry that supplied St. Oran's in 1868.

The child's name was Elsie Gray. Her family had brought her in with a fever, but a nurse sent her home before the fire began. Elsie was not counted among the forty-one patients listed in the official death record. Her discharge was never entered.

"My mother said they counted the dead and forgot the child who got out," Mrs. Arden told this newspaper. "The nurse who saved her never wrote it down. The hospital burned with forty-one names on the books, but forty-two people had been there."

Miss Morrow believes that omission explains why the ward continues to admit people. She proposes returning to the staircase and entering Elsie Gray's name and discharge date into the ward's intake slate. Dr. Saye has agreed to attempt the correction on Saturday morning.

Inspector Voss has found a second book mentioned in the fire report: the ward's discharge ledger. It was assumed destroyed. His description matches the book Miss Morrow saw inside the ward, still open on a desk beside the east window.
